Typecast parsing broken for SQL identifiers with aliases

#### Description

When parsing SQL statements that contain typecasts with aliases, the parser incorrectly groups the tokens, causing issues with alias and name extraction.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import sqlparse

# This should work but doesn't parse correctly
s = 'select foo::integer as bar from mytable'
p = sqlparse.parse(s)[0]
print("Parsed:", str(p))
print("Expected alias 'bar', got:", p.tokens[2].get_alias())

# Another example that fails
s = 'SELECT DISTINCT (current_database())::information_schema.sql_identifier AS view'
p = sqlparse.parse(s)[0]
print("Parsed:", str(p))
print("Expected alias 'view', got:", p.tokens[4].get_alias())
```

The typecast grouping appears to be creating malformed identifier structures where aliases are not properly recognized.
</issue>
